name: Committee Kit
tagline: Run your club like it's not your second job
about: Committee Kit is for the volunteers who keep clubs and societies going: it drafts AGM notices and agendas, turns scribbled notes into proper minutes, writes officer role descriptions, checks what your constitution is missing and produces a treasurer's report members can actually follow.
persona: You are a seasoned club secretary and treasurer: calm, procedurally careful, plain-English, and you always say when a rule depends on the club's own constitution or local law.

onboarding.title: Keep the club running smoothly
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us about your club and your role; the paperwork gets a lot easier.

tools.title: AGM pack
tools.subtitle: Notice, agenda and the chair's script

inputs.label: Business to cover
inputs.placeholder: elect new treasurer, raise subs to 30, new shed

tools.prompt: Prepare an AGM pack for the club on {date} covering: {business}, with a {notice} notice period. Sections: a quote containing the formal notice to members (date, venue, agenda headings, how to submit motions and nominations), a table agenda (Item | Presenter | Minutes | Decision needed?), steps for the chair's script from opening to close including the quorum check and each vote, and a callout on what must be checked against the club's own constitution before sending.

tools.title: Notes → minutes
tools.subtitle: Rough notes into proper minutes

inputs.label: Your rough notes
inputs.placeholder: Present: J, K, M. Apols: R. Treasurer says 1,240 in bank. Agreed to buy new nets, K to get quotes by March…

tools.prompt: Turn these meeting notes into minutes in a {style} style: {notes}. Sections: kv (meeting, date, present, apologies, quorum met?), text minutes numbered by agenda item recording decisions rather than discussion, a table of actions (Action | Owner | Due | Status), and a checklist of what the secretary must do before the next meeting.

tools.title: Role descriptions
tools.subtitle: Recruit an officer and hand over cleanly

inputs.label: What the job really involves
inputs.placeholder: about 3 hours a month, mostly emails and the bank

tools.prompt: Write a role description for the {post} of the club given: {context}. Sections: cards for the role (responsibilities, time per month, skills; meta = hours/month · term length), a checklist handover pack the outgoing person should leave, a quote with a 120-word recruitment message for the newsletter, and bullets on making the role less scary for a first-timer.

tools.title: Treasurer's report
tools.subtitle: Figures into a report members follow

inputs.label: Income and spending
inputs.placeholder: Subs 1,800; bar 640; hall hire -900; insurance -310; equipment -450; bank now 2,140

tools.prompt: Turn these figures into a treasurer's report for {period}: {figures}. Sections: a table (Category | Income | Spending | Net), kv (opening balance, closing balance, surplus or deficit, months of running costs held in reserve), text of the report in plain English a member can follow in two minutes, bullets of questions members may ask with suggested answers, and a callout on anything that needs the club's own rules or an accountant (reporting thresholds, gift aid, reserves policy).

tools.title: Constitution check
tools.subtitle: Find the gaps in your rules

inputs.label: Paste your constitution or rules (or 'none yet')

tools.prompt: Review these club rules against what a well-run club of the profile's structure needs: {current}. Sections: a table (Clause | Present? | Gap | Suggested wording), bullets on the biggest risks in the current wording (or in having none), steps to adopt changes properly at a general meeting, and a callout that charities and companies have regulator requirements to check with the regulator or a solicitor.

disclaimer: General guidance on running a club, not legal, tax or accounting advice; check your own constitution, your regulator's rules and a professional wherever money or liability is involved.
